patch.value: Token budgets bind one call and never compose: the orientation protocol the project prescribes costs 38k bytes and spends a third of it re-describing items the agent was already given

Measured on 2026-08-03 against the real tracker at 2,285 items using pm 2026.8.3.

The method was to price the protocol the project prescribes rather than the commands it ships. AGENTS.md tells an agent to orient with contracts --summary, context, search, list --status open, list --status in-progress, and next before creating work. Executed literally, that sequence costs:

  contracts --summary                 9,749 bytes
  context --limit 10                  9,144
  search <keywords> --limit 10        4,270
  list --status open --limit 20       4,832
  list --status in_progress --limit 20  812
  next                                9,660
  total                              38,467 bytes, roughly 9,600 tokens

Every one of those calls is individually well behaved. Each honours its own bound, each carries an omission receipt, several accept an explicit --token-budget. The defect is not in any of them. It is that the bounds do not compose: there is no unit of accounting above a single invocation.

The measurable consequence is redundancy. Extracting item ids from the four read surfaces: 110 total mentions resolve to 76 distinct items, so 31 percent of what the agent pays for is a repeat. 28 items appear on more than one surface; pm-doxj, pm-pbyu and pm-ki67py are each described three times in a single cold start. The agent is charged for the same fact once per surface that happens to rank it, and no surface knows the others ran.

There is no mechanism to prevent this. context exposes --after, which is a resume cursor for continuing one traversal, not a suppression set for facts already delivered. No read accepts a seen-set, a session identity, or a group budget. The token budget vocabulary is complete and correct at the call level and simply has no term above it.

Why this is the binding constraint now. The project has already established, in closed work, that budgets must be declared, that a budget must bind against the representation actually emitted, that omission must be receipted, and that a command must be able to report its own token cost. All of that is per call. At one agent the redundancy is a 31 percent tax on orientation. At a fleet it multiplies by the agent count, and the fleet-amortization work assumes a shared assembly can be reused across agents - which is the across-agent form of exactly the same question this raises within one agent.

The scale-symmetry requirement matters here. The redundancy is a property of ranking overlap, not of corpus size: it is present at 2,285 items and would be present at 30. Any fix must therefore be free at small scale, which rules out a persistent session index as the baseline mechanism and argues for the suppression set travelling with the request.

Scope is the composition law for output budgets across calls, and the deduplication it makes possible. Individual command budgets, the encoding used per surface, and cross-agent assembly sharing each have their own owners; this is the term that is missing between them.

A session or request-group identity can be supplied to successive reads, and a fact already served under that identity is not re-serialized in full; Suppressed repeats are represented by a reference the agent can resolve, not silently dropped, and the receipt says what was suppressed and why; A budget can be declared for a group of calls, and the group degrades deterministically when it is exhausted, exactly as a single call does today; The prescribed orientation sequence in AGENTS.md is measured end to end in CI, and the measurement is a ratchet that may only shrink; The mechanism composes with the fleet-level shared-assembly work rather than duplicating it: within-session dedupe and across-agent amortization use one representation; Small workspaces pay nothing for the machinery: at three items the orientation cost is unchanged or lower

The prescribed cold start is the single most-repeated read sequence in the product - every agent, every session, every fleet member pays it before doing any work. It is currently the largest unmeasured, unbounded cost in the system.
A session, not just a call, is the unit a token budget is declared against: an agent can state its whole orientation budget once, and pm spends it without paying twice for the same fact.
Every per-call budget mechanism the project has built is now in place and correct, which makes the missing composition law the binding constraint rather than a theoretical one.
